newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick shares fall as funds raise cash.
newsitem.headline: Barrick shares fall as funds raise cash.

text.p: Shares in Barrick Gold Corp fell in healthy trade on Wednesday, pressured by continued weakness in the gold market and the miner's refinancing efforts.
Analysts said the languishing market was likely forcing gold mutual fund managers to sell assets as jittery investors took their money elsewhere.

"When the redemptions get to a point, or shareholders are moving funds from those accounts, it gets to a point that they have to sell assets in order to raise additional cash," said Merrill Lynch analyst David Christensen.
"The only way to raise cash is to sell liquid and long-term holdings, such as Barrick, Newmont (Gold Co, Echo Bay (Mines Ltd ). They're all liquid stocks," he added.
Barrick shares were down as much as 0.75 to 31.50 before recovering slightly to trade down 0.60 at 31.65 on more than 675,000 shares. Ten block trades made up 415,000 shares of the volume.
Newmont and Echo Bay both traded near their 52-week lows on Wednesday.
Analysts said Barrick's refinancing efforts also pressured the stock.

"(Barrick is) in the process of establishing the financing, US$2 billion...that suggests that the company is going to continue acquiring other properties (or) companies... that tends to put pressure on the stock price," said analyst Todd Hinrichs at ABN AMRO Securities in Chicago.
Christensen said Barrick was well protected in the short term against languishing gold prices, but that the whole sector would be hurt in the long run if prices did not recover.

"The company has a very significant hedge position... (but) over the long term, without any upward movement in the gold price, it certainly hurts investors' enthusiasm for investing in gold stocks as a whole," Christensen said.
((Andrea Hopkins at Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8102 or e-mail andrea.hopkins@reuters.com))
